lean_source:
namespace Pipeline.Generated

/-- Number of lines in the input: each element of the stdin line list counts
    as one line (POSIX: `-l` writes the number of <newline> characters, which
    at the harness's line-level abstraction is the number of lines). -/
def countLines : List String → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | _ :: rest => countLines rest + 1

/-- Model of `wc -l` reading stdin: one output line holding the decimal line
    count, exit code 0. -/
def run (args stdin : List String) : List String × UInt32 :=
  ([Nat.repr (countLines stdin)], 0)

/-- The recursive line counter agrees with list length. -/
theorem countLines_eq_length (xs : List String) :
    countLines xs = xs.length := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x rest ih => simp [countLines, ih]

/-- The output is exactly one line: the decimal count of input lines. -/
theorem run_output_is_line_count (args stdin : List String) :
    (run args stdin).1 = [Nat.repr stdin.length] := by
  simp [run, countLines_eq_length]

/-- Exactly one line is written to standard output. -/
theorem run_single_output_line (args stdin : List String) :
    (run args stdin).1.length = 1 := by
  rfl

/-- Successful completion: exit status 0. -/
theorem run_exit_success (args stdin : List String) :
    (run args stdin).2 = 0 := by
  rfl

/-- Empty input has zero <newline> characters, so the count written is 0. -/
theorem run_empty_input (args : List String) :
    run args [] = (["0"], 0) := by
  rfl

/-- Adding one input line increments the reported count by one. -/
theorem run_cons_increments (args : List String) (l : String)
    (rest : List String) :
    (run args (l :: rest)).1 = [Nat.repr (rest.length + 1)] := by
  simp [run, countLines, countLines_eq_length]

/-- The count depends only on how many lines there are, not their contents. -/
theorem run_depends_only_on_length (args stdin other : List String)
    (h : stdin.length = other.length) :
    run args stdin = run args other := by
  simp [run, countLines_eq_length, h]

end Pipeline.Generated

spec_theorems.name: run_output_is_line_count
spec_theorems.informal: With -l, the standard output is a single entry containing the decimal count of <newline> characters, i.e. the number of input lines.

spec_theorems.name: run_single_output_line
spec_theorems.informal: Only the information requested by the specified option is reported: exactly one output line is written.

spec_theorems.name: run_empty_input
spec_theorems.informal: Empty standard input contains zero <newline> characters, so wc -l writes the count 0.

spec_theorems.name: run_cons_increments
spec_theorems.informal: Each additional input line increments the reported <newline> count by exactly one.

spec_theorems.name: run_depends_only_on_length
spec_theorems.informal: The -l count depends only on the number of lines, not on the bytes, words, or characters within them.
